nodes.label: Per-request nonce CSP requires dynamic rendering
nodes.rationale: A strict nonce CSP requires every route to be dynamically rendered (the root layout's force-dynamic cascades). Static rendering (force-static/ISR) stops Next applying per-request nonces and the enforced CSP would blank that route — such routes must move to a hash-based CSP. Metadata routes (manifest, apple-icon, opengraph-image) are separate segments where force-dynamic does NOT cascade, so they opt into force-static for the no-DB build.
nodes.norm_label: per-request nonce csp requires dynamic rendering

nodes.label: Dual email+IP rate limiting on auth endpoints
nodes.rationale: Login and signup are rate-limited by BOTH email and IP (either tripping blocks): per-email stops targeted brute force, per-IP stops spraying one password across many emails. Per-IP check is skipped when IP is unknown to avoid locking everyone out on a shared 'unknown' bucket from an XFF misconfig. Email is capped at RFC max 254 in the key so a giant value can't bloat the rate_limits PK.
nodes.norm_label: dual email+ip rate limiting on auth endpoints

nodes.label: Timing-safe credential check (no user enumeration)
nodes.rationale: authorize always runs a bcrypt compare against DUMMY_HASH on the no-user path so timing is identical regardless of whether the user exists — eliminating a user-enumeration oracle.

nodes.label: session_version per-user revocation
nodes.rationale: The jwt callback re-stamps sv from the AUTHORITATIVE DB session_version on trigger==='update' BEFORE the uid short-circuit, never from the client-supplied session payload (which is attacker-controllable). Trusting the client would let a revoked client re-stamp itself live and bypass revocation. The sv is checked on write paths to enforce per-user session revocation.

nodes.label: Provider email-verified trust policy
nodes.rationale: Google sets email_verified directly; GitHub's bundled provider returns the PRIMARY (not necessarily verified) email so it is confirmed via /user/emails (githubEmailVerified). Anything else is treated as unverified.

nodes.label: Lazy NextAuth config factory for link-nonce cookies
nodes.rationale: NextAuth config is a lazy factory rebuilt per request that receives the NextRequest on the /api/auth/* route handler, so the signIn callback can read per-provider link_nonce cookies via req.cookies. req is undefined from a server action's signIn()/unstable_update() — both correct. Account linking resolves atomically via single-use consumeLinkToken (no cookie delete, which is unreliable inside the Auth.js callback).
nodes.norm_label: lazy nextauth config factory for link-nonce cookies

nodes.label: Bare instrumentation module for secret-less CI build
nodes.rationale: instrumentation.ts keeps its module top-level bare (no imports, no env/DB reads); validateEnv is dynamically imported inside register() which runs at server START not during next build, so CI's secret-less build stays green. onRequestError is the Sentry-ready seam; it surfaces AggregateError nested causes (empty top-level message) and bounds the logged line to 500 chars.
nodes.norm_label: bare instrumentation module for secret-less ci build

nodes.label: requireVerifiedUserId write-path guard
nodes.rationale: All mutating server actions (logBrew/addBag/edits/deletes/toggles/comments) call requireVerifiedUserId as a fail-closed, revocation-aware write guard, then scope every SQL by user_id (ownership). Read-only paginated loaders use the softer getCurrentUserId. setDiscoverable uses requireUserId (verified-email not required to toggle indexing).

nodes.label: force-dynamic robots/sitemap for runtime AUTH_URL
nodes.rationale: robots.ts is force-dynamic so the sitemap URL reflects the runtime AUTH_URL via getPublicBaseUrl, not whatever (localhost) base was present at build time.

nodes.label: Drizzle-managed schema with raw pg runtime
nodes.rationale: Schema source of truth is lib/db/schema.ts compiled by drizzle-kit to drizzle/; runtime queries still use raw pg. db:setup applies additive non-destructive migrations + seeds if empty; db:reset is destructive. db/schema.sql is a frozen pre-Drizzle snapshot kept only as the fidelity oracle and must not be edited.
nodes.norm_label: drizzle-managed schema with raw pg runtime

nodes.label: Auth.js v5 (next-auth beta) authentication
nodes.rationale: Three sign-in methods (Credentials email+password, Google, GitHub) with JWT sessions. Browsing the feed/discover/bean/roaster pages is public; writing requires sign-in. OAuth identity keys on (provider, provider_account_id) in the accounts table, never on email.

nodes.label: Warm OKLCH design system / dark mode
nodes.rationale: Design tokens live as OKLCH CSS variables in app/globals.css, exposed to Tailwind via @theme inline. Dark mode flips a single .dark block that redefines the base palette; every shadcn semantic token is a var() ref, so light↔dark needs no per-component work.
nodes.norm_label: warm oklch design system / dark mode

nodes.label: Bean/Bag and Tasting/Brew data model
nodes.rationale: Two core objects: Bean/Bag is a rich catalog record created once (when owned it lives on the shelf with SCA score, bag weight, % left); Tasting/Brew is the fast everyday action logged against a bag.

nodes.label: Portable Claude Code tooling (skills/plugins/MCP)
nodes.rationale: Three layers: vendored skills in .agents/skills (zero install), plugins via enabledPlugins + restore-claude-env.sh, MCPs via .mcp.json. MCP approvals are always per-machine for security; the postgres MCP needs Docker + a running Postgres.
